newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Leopardstown aims to attract more race-goers.
newsitem.headline: Leopardstown aims to attract more race-goers.

text.p: Leopardstown racecourse in Dublin said on Wednesday it aimed to increase its attendances by 25 percent over the next three to five years.
In a statement, General Manager, John White, said Leopardstown endeavoured to increase its attendances from 160,000 to 200,000 over the period.
White also said that Leopardstown's proposed four million Irish pounds development plan had been approved by the Irish Horse Racing Authority.
Last week the IHA announced it had created a Capital Development Fund of 30 million punts for Irish racecourses.
"Leopardstown's dynamic plan which has been been approved by the IHA will include a major revamp of the entrance, general enclosures and facilities at the racecourse," White said.
White said that prize money to the value of 360,000 Irish pounds would be available at the 1996 Christmas Festival meeting at Leopardstown.
Last year's Christmas Festival meeting at the south-Dublin venue was lost due to bad weather. -- Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 6603377
